title: Daniel C. Kim v. Korean Southwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC approved the recommendation that the complaint was no longer in order after Kim and others reportedly withdrew from the PCA to form an independent congregation. It made no merits ruling.
first_summary: Daniel C. Kim’s complaint against Korean Southwest Presbytery was declared no longer in order after Kim and others withdrew from the PCA to form an independent congregation. The SJC approved the committee’s recommendation under BCO 43-1, which requires a complainant to be a communing member subject to the jurisdiction of the court complained against.
summary: The SJC did not reach the unidentified action challenged by Daniel C. Kim against Korean Southwest Presbytery. It approved a recommendation that the complaint was no longer in order because Kim and others reportedly withdrew from the PCA to form an independent congregation. Under BCO 43-1, a complainant must be a communing member subject to the respondent court’s jurisdiction; no merits ruling was made.
